APPR-ATTESTATION.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 4 §5.2, finding A-6. A review is of an artifact, never of a publisher; reviews travel like apps do. Plan open question 4 — whether a 'concern' verdict raises the bar or only informs — is decided here: raising it gives a trusted reviewer a unilateral brake, desirable against a hostile author and a denial-of-service surface if that reviewer is compromised.

APPR-DEVICE-AMBIENT.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 0, finding A-1. device.inventory/device.diagnostics register with null capability and reach real host state; holder is app:${appId}, making polling a zero-permission cross-app side channel. Require a capability or return only host-neutral facts, and drop holder from the unprivileged path. The load-bearing finding: a risk model whose zero point is not zero is incoherent before it starts.

APPR-EVALUATE.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 3 §6. Sans-IO in packages/protocol: the host gathers evidence, the function decides. Earns an executable table plus Layer-3 vectors in conformance/vectors/approval.json, but deliberately not a TLA+ model — a model becomes necessary only if the override path grows states, which is a design smell worth resisting. Thresholds T1..T4 and K are product calls informed by the sim campaign (plan open question 3); this item states where they plug in.

APPR-FIRST-SEEN.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 2, finding A-4 and §5.1. (appId, publisherKey, packageHash) -> firstSeenAt, written on catalog ingest and not subject to the seven-day catalog TTL. A publisher-signed publishedAt is attacker-chosen, so age must come from observers; a changed package is a new hash and resets its own clock. The cheapest item in the plan and the one that makes 'unchanged for a minimum period' measurable at all.

APPR-FLOOR-PROBE.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 0. A hostile fixture asserting a capabilities: [] app can observe nothing about the host or other apps. Written before APPR-DEVICE-AMBIENT: it is the statement of the invariant, and its absence is why A-1 survived a security review.

APPR-OPTIONAL-CAPS.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 2, finding A-7. Declining an optional capability still launches. Today launchWithCapabilityReview rejects an empty set, which teaches that declining is how you fail to launch. Rides the same formatVersion: 2 change as CAP-MANIFEST-V2 and should land with it, not as a second format bump.

APPR-OVERRIDE-UX.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 3 §4. An unmet requirement is a statement of what could not be verified, never a refusal — a local-first platform that hard-blocks its owner is dishonest, and they will sideload with less information than the dialog had. Proceeding needs an explicit, distinctly-worded action and writes the unmet set into the ConsentRecord. A requirement nobody can override is a central gatekeeper by the back door; one that a single identical tap clears is a formality wearing a control's clothes.

APPR-REVIEW-UX.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 1, finding A-3. No new gates in this phase — it makes the existing dialog honest, which is most of the user-visible benefit at a fraction of the risk of getting thresholds wrong.

APPR-REVIEWER-SET.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 4 §5.2. An attestation counts only if the reviewer key is in the user's own list; no global score, no badge, no credential. K distinct keys are trivially Sybil-able, so the host refuses to count two keys that arrived in the same import, or any key from the app's own publisher, and displays the rest for the user to judge. Claiming to have solved Sybil resistance here would be the dishonest move. Deliberately last: the largest, most speculative piece, and the only one that cannot be validated without other people. Bootstrapping a reviewer set is explicitly unsettled (plan §11).

APPR-RISK-CLASS.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 1, finding A-2. specs/spec-cap/registry/capability-risk.json plus generator and capability-risk.gen.ts, the same shape and discipline as device-classes.json, so revising the assignment is a data change. The four-class assignment in §3.1 is argued, not measured, and is reviewed as part of this item.

APPR-SPEC-RISK.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 5. Risk class in the miniapp-sdk.md table, LIMITATIONS §7 residual, and the F4 cross-reference.

APPR-TIER.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 1 §3.2. Not a sum: ten benign capabilities are not one sensitive one. The promotion rule catches the composition per-capability review misses — a microphone alone is a recorder, lxmf:send alone is a messenger, together they are a wiretap. Plan open question 1 asks whether max + promotion is the right function; validate against generated hostile app shapes before APPR-EVALUATE hardens it.

APPR-TRUST-DEGREE.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 2, finding A-5 and §5.3. TrustStore already records source: qr|paste|manual and no code reads it. Promote it to direct/imported/introduced and surface it; isTrusted gains a degree argument. This is where the 'paste this identity string' lure stops being a coin flip: a lure can reach imported and cannot reach direct.

APPR-UPDATE-DELTA.notes: app-approval-risk-plan.md Phase 2, finding A-7 and hostile-author scenario HA-11. An update adding a capability must not auto-activate; the delta and its risk are named.

BUG-AUDIT-FIX-POSTINSTALL.notes: npm audit fix reorders the tree while installing, so apps/host-desktop's postinstall runs when its own @electron/get is not resolvable; the install aborts, the lockfile is untouched, and fix.mjs ignores applyFixes().ok and reports 'Nothing was fixable without a breaking upgrade.'

BUG-ELECTRON-BUILDER-VERSION.notes: d6e4d364 made the Electron binary download best-effort at postinstall, so on CI electron is not present in node_modules and electron-builder cannot resolve the ^43.3.0 range: 'Electron version ^43.3.0 is a range, not a fixed version'. Pin the exact version, which is what electron-builder needs to fetch platform binaries itself.

BUG-LXMF-COVERAGE.notes: Reproduced on a clean checkout of main at 856957d2 with an unmodified coverage-ratchet.json and packages/lxmf-ts byte-identical to origin/main: 'packages/lxmf-ts functions: 72.5 < floor 73.33'. The floor is committed higher than the code achieves, so check:ci-base reports 15/16 static-analysis gates on an untouched tree. Either add function coverage in packages/lxmf-ts to clear 73.33 or, if the floor was set from a run that measured a different file set, correct the baseline with a recorded reason. A standing red gate trains people to ignore the gate. Distinct from the derived GATE-COVERAGE item, which only reports that the check is failing right now and disappears when it passes: this row carries the diagnosis and the open decision between the two fixes, and is closed with evidence for whichever one is taken.

BUG-MINIAPP-IDENTITY-BACKEND.notes: Reproduced locally: the chat example launches, logs 'broker denied identity.destinationHash', never emits a widgetTree, and the 20s waitFor fails. Same signature fails nightly desktop-soak and CI ios-sim. Cause: 3c8b6c13 made createWorkletMiniappHost always install createAppScopedIdentityBackend, whose identityFor() throws 'No installation identity is available; start the node first' when neither getInstallationIdentity nor getPublisherIdentity is supplied. Before that commit worklet-core passed no identityBackend, so the runtime's always-available stub in miniapp-runtime/src/host/layer-1-base.ts was used. Fix is a product decision: either these harnesses must supply an installation identity (keeps the boundary strict), or the host needs a defined behaviour when no node has started. Do not restore a derivable stub identity — that is the boundary 3c8b6c13 removed.

BUG-REACT-DOM-MISMATCH.notes: Dependabot fe9d40f5 bumped react-dom to 19.2.8 alone. Expo SDK 57 bundledNativeModules pins react and react-dom at 19.2.3 and react-native 0.86.2 peers react ^19.2.3, but .npmrc legacy-peer-deps=true hid the conflict at install time. Realign with npx expo install --fix per AGENTS.md.

BUG-RESOURCE-SEGMENTATION.notes: split/segmentIndex/totalSegments were hardcoded false/1/1 in resource/layer-1.ts, so any payload past RNS MAX_EFFICIENT_SIZE (16777215) stopped at one segment. Sender now cuts and chains segments sharing one originalHash; receiver accumulates by originalHash and concludes on the last. Verified against the pinned Python RNS 0.9.5 echo peer at 20MB (2 segments) and 104857600 bytes (7 segments), the nightly resource-interop-100mb configuration.

CAP-HOSTILE-PROBES.notes: capability-scoping-plan.md Phase 0. Listed last in the plan's table but written first: the probe is the regression proof, and three of the four Phase 0 defects are one-line fixes whose absence of a test is why they survived a security review.

CAP-TTL.notes: capability-scoping-plan.md Phase 1, audit finding F-5. Typed bug rather than feature: SPEC-CAP already states no grant is immortal and the machinery is model-checked, so this is a conformance gap. FN-A1-ANDROID-E5.notes: freenet-simulator-first-work-plan.md A1. The harness already requires wasmExecuted plus kill and timing measurements, and ANDROID_BENCHMARK_RECORD=1 writes measured-worker.json and updates s4-support-matrix.json. What is missing is a committed emulator run. Simulator evidence may close software readiness but must never be relabelled as physical-device evidence.

FN-A2-IOS-WASM.notes: freenet-simulator-first-work-plan.md A2. test:ios-sim:wasm parses the Maestro hierarchy for numeric timings with no hardcoded pass, and IOS_BENCHMARK_RECORD=1 updates the S4 matrix; committed measurements remain pending a simulator run. Keep reviewed simulator evidence separate from any later physical-device result, and wire the required form into test:ios-sim:required.

FN-DEVICE-CONFIRM.notes: freenet-simulator-first-work-plan.md §8. One representative Android phone and one iPhone; borrowed is fine and no dedicated fleet is needed. Checks: WASM executes inside the BareKit Worker, the watchdog kills the hostile worker under moderate load, 10-20 spawn/kill cycles without false positives, one foreground/background transition, remote-node disclosure/refusal/revocation, no credentials in device logs, and a short read-only connection to a user-controlled node. Run only if mobile Freenet support is intended to ship; it does not block desktop/headless release or the simulator-verified milestones.

FN-E1-LIVE-EVIDENCE.notes: freenet-simulator-first-work-plan.md E1, and the unmet F1 exit criterion in freenet.md: publish from host A and force installation on host B, plus the live S2 series and retrieval after a client or node restart, on one approved non-sensitive test contract. Starts only after explicit approval for irreversible public metadata. Review ignored raw results before deliberately updating committed evidence, and never copy an incomplete run over a gate artifact.

FN-E2-WRITE-INTEROP.notes: freenet-simulator-first-work-plan.md E2. The read half passed: the TS adapter read the live Atlas CBOR index through a localhost node. The write half needs application authority as well as permission to publish — preferably an upstream-approved Atlas test record or curator key, another independently developed app with a user-writable contract, or an explicitly approved rejected update recorded honestly as request-and-rejection evidence. Even a rejected or idempotent update publishes public operation metadata. No simulator or isolated testnet substitutes for this.

FN-F-DISTRIBUTION.notes: freenet-simulator-first-work-plan.md F, and S5 in freenet.md. Interim decision 2026-07-29: ship posture 2 (user-supplied supervised binary), keeping posture 1 (external node) documented. Postures 3 and 4 need fresh upstream-artifact verification, platform package sizes, upgrade/rollback rules, clean-host execution tests, and — on macOS — Developer ID signing, hardened-runtime verification, notarization, stapling, and Gatekeeper verification, with an explicit Windows posture. Signing services cannot be replaced by simulator evidence, so F4 stays gated.

HA-P0-BASELINE.notes: hostile-author-plan.md P0. The plan's 'Today' column is an unverified code read; this item replaces every guess with a measured verdict in conformance/hostile-authors/README.md. Deliberately separate and first: writing fixtures before measuring the baseline produces fixtures that encode assumptions, and several 'likely finding' guesses will be wrong in both directions.

HA-P1-TRANSCRIPT.notes: hostile-author-plan.md P1 §5. Host chrome emits a structured record for every consent moment, and fixtures assert against the record rather than pixels — this is the oracle that makes an INFORMED verdict machine-checked rather than a belief about what the UI probably says. Buys the fixture oracle, a user-visible 'what did I approve' log, and a forcing function: authority conferred without a record is authority the user was never told about. Covers Surface 1/2/4/5 scenarios and wires test:hostile-authors into CI (add the npm script and the conformance/README.md and docs/README.md rows with it).

HA-P2-RENDER-ORACLE.verify: npx vitest run packages/miniapp-runtime/test/ui-validate-chrome-lexicon.test.ts && npm run test:chrome
HA-P2-RENDER-ORACLE.notes: hostile-author-plan.md P2, Surface 3. Layer A is a deterministic validator pass in ui/validate.ts rejecting reserved chrome vocabulary, chrome-imitating layout signatures, and secret-solicitation patterns — proposed CHROME-R7 (reserved lexicon) and CHROME-R8 (no secret solicitation). Layer B is snapshot geometry proving confirmations render outside the app surface and cannot be occluded, which is the 'snapshot-based check' SPEC-CHROME's own text is waiting on. Layer A is where the value is; Layer B is what closes the spec. HA-21 — an app asking the user to type their recovery phrase — is the highest-severity scenario in the catalog and needs no capabilities at all.

HA-P3-FINDINGS.notes: hostile-author-plan.md P3: confirmation rate limiting, host-derived confirmation summaries, confusable-name flagging, capability-delta review on update, per-app moderation granularity. Exit is that every finding is BLOCKED, INFORMED-with-transcript, or CONTAINED-with-a-metric. Scope may overlap APPR-UPDATE-DELTA; close whichever lands second against the other's evidence rather than duplicating the fix.

HA-P4-SCOPED-EGRESS.notes: hostile-author-plan.md P4. HA-30 (granted lxmf:send used to ship the contact list) and HA-36 (benign until a remote flag arrives) are the plan's load-bearing scenarios: they cannot be resolved by better dialogs, only by EgressOffer. Written red now and standing as the acceptance test for the scoping work. Exit rewrites security-review.md F4 from an accepting sentence into an enumerated residual and updates LIMITATIONS §7.

ID-APPSCOPE.notes: identity.sign is broker-reachable (host/layer-1-handlers-core.ts) but no shipping host supplies an identityBackend, so MiniappHost falls back to the stub in host/layer-1-base.ts: destinationHash is app:<appId>:<publisher-prefix> and sign() returns the literal text signed:<payload>. Only simulation-adapter.ts wires a real backend. Fix by deriving the app-scoped identity from the installation identity per decision 3 of docs/linked-devices-plan.md, so an app on two of a user's machines is two peers.

ID-DEVICES-RELABEL.notes: Decision 5 of docs/linked-devices-plan.md. The Devices panel lists cameras, microphones, and sensors; to a user 'my devices' means their phone and laptop, which is what the linked-installation screen will show. Relabel the peripheral chrome to 'Hardware access' and reserve 'Your devices' for installations. User-visible label strings only: device:<class>:<tier> capabilities, SPEC-DEVICE, the Device Manager, and all wire values keep their spelling. Must land before the first linked-installation screen so the two never ship sharing a word.

ID-JOURNAL.notes: Content-addressed records signed by the emitting installation certificate, deduplicated by record hash, bounded by the existing propagation and multipart limits. Records are proposals only; nothing applies itself. See docs/linked-devices-plan.md. Waits on ID-SIBLING-GATE so the record shape is dictated by the policy boundary rather than the transport.

ID-LINKED-MODE.notes: Enabling migrates host and app serving destinations to the installation identity while the account/publisher hash stays stable. Disabling is not offered. Importing a backup or recovery words must not silently enable linked mode. Also settle the user-facing name: the Devices panel already means peripherals. See docs/linked-devices-plan.md.

ID-ROSTER.notes: Persist verified TPDV certificates, announce under the account-derived aspect, and merge valid certificates into a local roster. Both pairing directions per docs/linked-devices-plan.md. linked-installation.ts supplies the format and is consumed by nothing today.

ID-SIBLING-CHROME.notes: SiblingDecisionGate decides but applies nothing. Remaining: chrome rendering held proposals with grant and revoke controls, a durable SiblingProposalStore replacing createInMemorySiblingProposalStore, and the code turning an apply verdict into a write to FileModerationStore and TrustStore. Must state in the UI that removing an installation from the roster stops fan-out but does not revoke globally — offline installations learn of removal only when they next sync.

ID-SIBLING-GATE.notes: Default deny. A journal record from another installation is a proposal: verified, stored, surfaced, applied only where the receiving installation holds a grant for that class (sibling:moderation, sibling:trust, sibling:apps, sibling:messages), revocable per sibling and per class. Capability grants themselves have no sibling class and must be proven not to travel. See decision 2 of docs/linked-devices-plan.md. PREREQUISITE CHANGE 2026-08-10: the gate no longer waits on the journal. It is the only piece that encodes the user-authority property the whole feature exists to provide, and it is buildable now against an in-memory journal because verifying a record needs only the certificate format, which ships. Building it first lets the policy boundary define the record shape; building it last lets the transport define it and refits the security property afterwards. ID-JOURNAL now waits on the gate so the transport lands into a proven boundary. SCOPE AT CLOSE: the gate — classes, default deny, per-sibling/per-class grants, hold-not-drop, backlog release, revocation, rejection of unknown class/non-sibling/self/duplicate, and the closed vocabulary that cannot carry a capability grant. The chrome and the code that applies an apply-verdict to the moderation and trust stores are tracked separately as ID-SIBLING-CHROME.

LINT-RUFF-CONFIG.notes: scripts/languages/check.mjs runs ruff from the repo root without --config, and ruff only discovers ruff.toml/.ruff.toml/pyproject.toml beside the file or in an ancestor — never .config/ruff.toml. Nothing else in the tree references that file either, so its select = [E, F, I, UP, B] and line-length = 100 have never applied: the gate has been running ruff's defaults (E4/E7/E9/F, line-length 88). Passing --config .config/ruff.toml turns on I/UP/B across every tracked .py file, so it needs its own baselining decision rather than a one-line change.

MINIAPP-APP-TO-APP.notes: Sequenced behind MINIAPP-CONCURRENT. A brokered, separately granted channel with the destination app named on the grant screen. Shared storage is out of scope. Ledger row MLC-APP-TO-APP.

MINIAPP-BACKGROUND-ANDROID.notes: mobile-lifecycle-plan.md candidate 2; ledger row MLC-BACKGROUND-ANDROID. Android already runs a foreground service for mesh participation and nothing prevents mini-app execution inside it, so the API is the easy part and the rationing is the design: what a background grant costs in terms a grant screen can state honestly, who loses when budgets are oversubscribed, and whether this is Android-only or a capability that does less on iOS. The honest option is to expose it and record the asymmetry in platform-capabilities-status.md rather than level down to iOS. MLC-BACKGROUND-IOS stays os-imposed until Apple changes policy.

MINIAPP-CONCURRENT.notes: The mobile OS constrains the host process, not mini-apps within it: iOS suspends the whole app and Android needs a foreground service, but neither limits how many sandboxes a running host may hold. MiniappHost nonetheless keeps a single `active: ActiveApp | null` slot (packages/miniapp-runtime/src/host/layer-1-base.ts), so launching a second app stops the first. The dev-preview slot already runs a second MiniappHost concurrently in the same worklet (packages/worklet-core/src/miniapp-host-shared-core.mjs), which is the existence proof that the platform, not the OS, imposes the limit. Replace the single slot with per-app instances, route broker traffic and budgets per app, and give the shells a switcher. Ledger row MLC-CONCURRENT-APPS in mobile-lifecycle-ledger.json.

MINIAPP-LIFECYCLE-EVENTS.notes: mobile-lifecycle-plan.md candidate 1; ledger row MLC-LIFECYCLE-EVENTS. The host already receives suspend-node and resume-node and acts on them; the sandbox is told nothing, which is why authors/12-limits-and-budgets.md imposes a persist-on-every-write tax on every app. The grace window is what makes it non-trivial: a suspend handler runs inside the same short window the host uses to quiesce interfaces, so it needs a hard budget and an overrunning app must be killed rather than delaying the quiesce. That argues for a strictly bounded synchronous checkpoint, not a general onSuspend running arbitrary app code.

MINIAPP-SCHEDULED-WAKE.notes: mobile-lifecycle-plan.md candidate 3; ledger row MLC-SCHEDULED-WAKE. iOS fetch/processing wake budgets already exist and are spent on propagation sync. The scarce resource is per-host, not per-app: a phone with six installed apps cannot give each one periodic wake-ups, so the rationing rule is the deliverable and the API follows from it.

WORK-EFFORT.notes: Within a class, ranking falls through unblock-count and added-date to alphabetical ID, so it cannot tell a 5-file fix from a 164-file campaign. The imported ratchet items make this concrete: no-floating-promises (5 files) and no-unnecessary-condition (164 files) rank adjacently on identical signals. Options: an explicit effort field on the item, or deriving one from the file count work:import already computes. Whichever lands, add the ordering rule to the ranking tests and to the 'why this one' output.

WORK-UNATTENDED.notes: The nine RQ soaks are not nine decisions: they are one action (npm run validate:mac -- --stage 8 --plan-duration) followed by up to 72 hours of waiting. work:next allocates attention, but its top answer currently costs almost none, and it presents the batch as a queue to pick from. Marking such items unattended would let work:next say 'start these, then do this' and rank the hands-on item second. Relates to work:done --from-log, which already assumes soaks run outside the tool.
